place.t_kin_village: a village where your kin live
ev.t_pirates.title: Pirates
ev.t_pirates.text: On the second day at sea two light galleys shot out from behind a headland. Within the hour Cilician pirates owned the deck. The passengers were herded to the stern while the pirates sized them up: who would fetch a ransom, and who was easier to sell at the slave market on Delos.
ev.t_pirates.ransom.success: The letter arrived, and your family raised the money by selling nearly everything. You were put ashore alive, penniless - and free.
ev.t_pirates.ransom.failure: The ransom didn't come in time. You were taken to Delos and sold like a bale of wool. Now you have a master.
ev.t_pirates.boast.success: You laughed at them, recited poetry at them, and promised to come back one day with a fleet. The pirates decided you were someone important, took a modest ransom and let you go with honor.
ev.t_pirates.boast.failure: Your nerve didn't impress them. “Sharp tongues sell well to rhetoric schools,” said the captain, and on Delos you were the first to go.
ev.t_pirates.escape.success: On a moonless night you slipped overboard and reached the shore clinging to an empty wineskin. Fishermen found you on the sand at dawn - without a coin, but free.
ev.t_pirates.escape.failure: They spotted you and fished you out with boathooks. Runaways aren't ransomed - they're sold. Within a week you had a master.
ev.t_pirates.join.ok: The captain liked your strength and gave you an oar and a share of the plunder. There's no road back to an honest life now - not for a while.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.title: A Fleet on the Horizon
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.text: A Roman fleet is sweeping the sea from coast to coast, and pirate nests are burning one after another. Their commander has proclaimed: those who surrender will get land and pardon; the rest will share the fate of the captured.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.surrender.ok: You laid down your weapons. They gave you a plot in a quiet valley far from the sea. Hands used to an oar are learning to hold a plow.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.keep_raiding.success: Your galley slipped past the Roman ships with rich plunder. You got away and vanished into a port town with a full purse.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.keep_raiding.failure: The Romans caught you off a headland. You were pulled wounded from the water - and the captured pirate became a slave.
ev.t_earthquake.title: Earthquake
ev.t_earthquake.text: At dawn the ground roared and heaved. Walls cracked, roof tiles rained into the street, and a knocked-over brazier started a fire somewhere. A scream comes from under the rubble of the house next door.
ev.t_earthquake.text.rome: At dawn the ground roared and heaved, like the time Campania shook. Walls cracked, roof tiles rained into the street, and a knocked-over brazier started a fire somewhere. A scream comes from under the rubble of the house next door.
ev.t_earthquake.text.egypt: At dawn the ground roared and shuddered - in Egypt, where it rarely happens, people cry out that the gods are angry. Mud-brick walls crumble, and a scream comes from under the rubble of the house next door.
ev.t_earthquake.dig.success: With bare hands you dug out your neighbor and his children. That family will remember you in their prayers for the rest of their lives.
ev.t_earthquake.dig.failure: The wall came down again and pinned your leg. Others pulled the neighbor out, and you limped for a long time.
ev.t_earthquake.save_goods.ok: You got everything valuable out before the looters came. The neighbors remember who dug through rubble and who dug through their own chests.
ev.t_earthquake.run_free.success: In the dust and screaming nobody saw you slip out of the gate. They'll count you among the dead under the rubble - the best gift fate could give.
ev.t_earthquake.run_free.failure: You were seized at the city gate. Your master decided you'd tried to profit from disaster - and he was right.
ev.t_earthquake.leave.ok: You gathered what survived and went to your kin. Let the earth shake without you.
ev.t_patron_falls.title: The Patron Falls
ev.t_patron_falls.text: {npc}, your patron, has fallen from grace overnight: accusation, trial, confiscation. Yesterday petitioners crowded {g=npc_sex:his|her} door; today the street is empty. Everyone connected with {g=npc_sex:him|her} is under suspicion - you included.
ev.t_patron_falls.text.rome: {npc}, your patron, has fallen out of favor with the powerful overnight: accusation, trial, confiscation. Yesterday clients crowded {g=npc_sex:his|her} door at dawn; today the street is empty. Everyone connected with {g=npc_sex:him|her} is under suspicion - you included.
ev.t_patron_falls.text.egypt: {npc}, your patron, has lost the favor of the royal court in Alexandria overnight: accusation, confiscation, guards at the door. Everyone connected with {g=npc_sex:him|her} is under suspicion - you included.
ev.t_patron_falls.stand.success: You brought {g=npc_sex:him|her} food and spoke up when others kept silent. The storm passed, and {npc} won't forget who stood by.
ev.t_patron_falls.stand.failure: Loyalty cost dearly: you were dragged in for questioning and part of your property was seized. {npc} went into exile, and the tie was cut.
ev.t_patron_falls.denounce.ok: Your testimony helped the prosecution and you were generously rewarded. But in the street people whisper a word behind your back that's worse than any curse.
ev.t_patron_falls.vanish.ok: You went to your kin, abandoning half your affairs. No one touched you - they simply forgot you.
ev.t_midwife_accused.title: Accused of Poisoning
ev.t_midwife_accused.text: A woman from a rich household died in childbirth, though you did everything you could. Her family is shouting up and down the street that your herbs are poison and you're a witch. Accusations like that end in court - and sometimes worse.
ev.t_midwife_accused.defend: Call the women you've helped as witnesses
ev.t_midwife_accused.defend.success: Twenty women came to court with children in their arms - every one of them delivered by you. The judges fell silent and the accusers left.
ev.t_midwife_accused.defend.failure: The witnesses were too frightened to come. You were fined, your name disgraced, and you'll long remember the stone thrown from the crowd.
ev.t_midwife_accused.flee.ok: You left at night with nothing but your bag of herbs. There are women giving birth in your kin's village too - and no one there knows your story.
ev.t_midwife_accused.altar: Take refuge at an altar and swear by the gods
ev.t_midwife_accused.altar.success: You swore a terrible oath at the altar, and the priests spoke up for you. The dead woman's family backed down - no one argues with the gods.
ev.t_midwife_accused.altar.failure: They heard the oath but didn't believe it. The disgrace stayed, and your patients now go to someone else.
ev.t_sycophant.title: The Sycophant
ev.t_sycophant.text: A man with an oily smile approaches you - a well-known sycophant. He has “happened to learn” that you supposedly spoke disrespectfully of the gods and hid part of your income. He's willing to forget it - for a fee. Otherwise it's court before hundreds of jurors.
ev.t_sycophant.note: In Athens “sycophants” were people who profited from denunciations and threats of prosecution: any citizen could bring a public charge, and this was used for extortion. There was a special lawsuit against sycophants, but fear of them is a constant theme in the speeches and comedies of the 5th-4th centuries BC.
ev.t_sycophant.pay.ok: He counted the coins and bowed. You hope never to see him again - but his kind always come back.
ev.t_sycophant.court: Hire a speechwriter and fight it
ev.t_sycophant.court.success: You learned the speech written for you by heart. The jurors laughed at the accuser and acquitted you by a huge majority.
ev.t_sycophant.court.failure: The jurors believed him, not you. A huge fine and disgrace before the whole city.
ev.t_sycophant.countersue.success: You dragged all his past extortions into the light. The court convicted him, and people call you the one who wasn't afraid.
ev.t_sycophant.countersue.failure: He had good witnesses, and yours had poor memories. You lost and paid for your boldness.
ev.t_sycophant.flee: Move to the countryside, far from the city
ev.t_sycophant.flee.ok: You moved to a village. Sycophants don't like dusty roads - but you can forget about your business in the city.
ev.t_sycophant_again.title: He's Back
ev.t_sycophant_again.text: The sycophant is at your door again, with the same smile. “Circumstances have changed. I need a little more.”
ev.t_sycophant_again.pay.ok: You paid. Now you know it will never end.
ev.t_sycophant_again.fight.success: You gathered his other victims, and together you beat him. He won't come to anyone's door again.
ev.t_sycophant_again.fight.failure: The court took his side again. You lost money; he lost nothing.
ev.t_games_victory.title: The Victor's Wreath
ev.t_games_victory.text: You won the footrace at the local games, and the whole city is talking about you. Your old trainer swears that with legs like yours you could win at Olympia: ten months of training, the journey to Elis, and eternal glory - or disgrace before all of Hellas.
ev.t_games_victory.text.athens: You won the footrace at the Panathenaia and took home an amphora of sacred oil. Your old trainer swears you could win at Olympia too - and Athens feeds an Olympic victor at public expense in the Prytaneion for the rest of his life. Or it's disgrace before all of Hellas.
ev.t_games_victory.text.egypt: You won the footrace at the Ptolemaia in Alexandria, and the whole city is talking about you. Your old trainer swears you could win at Olympia: Alexandrians have brought wreaths home from there before. Ten months of training, a voyage overseas - and eternal glory or disgrace.
ev.t_games_victory.olympia.success: You touched the finishing stone first. An olive wreath, your name cried by the herald - and at home they welcome you as a hero, as if you'd won a war.
ev.t_games_victory.olympia.failure: You came fourth. Olympia gives no prize for second place, let alone fourth - and you return home quietly.
ev.t_games_victory.hire_out: Compete for another city, for money
ev.t_games_victory.hire_out.ok: A rich city paid to have the herald announce you as theirs. Good money - but back home, they say, people want to tear down your statue.
ev.t_games_victory.settle.ok: You hung the wreath over the hearth. Every tavern in the quarter will pour you a free cup until you're old.
ev.t_hetaira.title: The Hetaira from Miletus
ev.t_hetaira.text: You've fallen in love with a hetaira from Miletus - educated, witty, a match for any philosopher in argument. But she isn't Athenian, and by law your children won't be citizens. Your father has already picked out a bride from a good family, with a dowry.
ev.t_hetaira.note: Under Pericles' law of 451 BC, only those with two Athenian parents could be citizens of Athens. Pericles himself lived with Aspasia of Miletus, and the Assembly made their son a citizen only as an exception, after Pericles' legitimate sons had died.
ev.t_hetaira.live_together.ok: She moved into your house, and it filled with guests, debates and laughter. Your father stopped visiting, and a character suspiciously like you has appeared in the comedies.
ev.t_hetaira.citizen_bride: Marry an Athenian, as your father wishes
ev.t_hetaira.citizen_bride.ok: The wedding went as it should. Your wife is quiet and kind. And sometimes you walk past a certain house without raising your eyes.
ev.t_hetaira.both.success: Your wife pretends not to know, the hetaira pretends not to be jealous. As long as everyone pretends, life is bearable.
ev.t_hetaira.both.failure: The secret came out at the very first banquet. Your father-in-law is furious, your wife silent for weeks, and the city laughs.
ev.t_hetaira_children.title: Illegitimate
ev.t_hetaira_children.text: {npc}, your child by the Milesian woman, has grown up, and now the full weight of the law comes down: {g=npc_sex:he isn't entered on the deme's roll of citizens|no citizen will take her as a wife}, and others jeer at {g=npc_sex:him|her} as a bastard. {npc} looks at you and waits to see what you'll do.
ev.t_hetaira_children.petition: Petition the Assembly for an exception
ev.t_hetaira_children.petition.success: The Assembly heard you out and voted: {npc} is Athenian. You wept on the Pnyx and weren't ashamed.
ev.t_hetaira_children.petition.failure: The Assembly refused. The law is the law, they said - even for those you love.
ev.t_hetaira_children.send_abroad: Send {g=npc_sex:him|her} to seek a fortune overseas
ev.t_hetaira_children.send_abroad.ok: You gave money and letters to friends in the colonies. There, nobody asks about your mother - they ask what you can do.
ev.t_hetaira_children.accept.ok: You said that's how the world is. {npc} nodded, but left without a word.
ev.t_epikleros.title: The Heiress
ev.t_epikleros.text: Your father has died leaving no sons. By law you're now an epikleros - an heiress who passes, together with the property, to the nearest male relative. Your father's cousin, twice your age, has already laid claim: to the land, the house - and to you. Even if you're married.
ev.t_epikleros.note: In Athens a daughter with no brothers became an epikleros: her nearest paternal kinsman could claim her in marriage along with the estate, and her existing marriage could be dissolved for it. The law aimed to keep property within the family; sons of such a marriage became their grandfather's heirs.
ev.t_epikleros.accept.ok: You entered your kinsman's house as his wife. Your father's land stayed in the family, and one day it will pass to your sons. It's the only thought that warms you.
ev.t_epikleros.dowry_deal: Persuade him to take the land and give you a dowry
ev.t_epikleros.dowry_deal.success: He thought it over and agreed: the land matters more to him than a young wife with a temper. You got a dowry and the freedom to choose.
ev.t_epikleros.dowry_deal.failure: He just laughed. A month later you entered his house as his wife - without consent and without joy.
ev.t_epikleros.fight: Fight for your marriage in court
ev.t_epikleros.fight.success: You and your husband proved the estate was small and the kinsman wanted only the land. The archon left you with your husband, and part of the property to you.
ev.t_epikleros.fight.failure: The archon ruled by the letter of the law. Your marriage is dissolved, and you pass to your kinsman along with your father's house.
ev.t_epikleros.flee.ok: You fled beyond the borders of Attica, leaving behind both the inheritance and your old name. Free - but in Athens they speak of you in whispers.
ev.t_delator.title: The Informer
ev.t_delator.text: At a dinner you made a careless joke about the emperor - everyone laughed. Three days later an informer charged you with treason against the majesty of the emperor. Cases like this end in exile or confiscation, and the informer gets a quarter of the convicted man's property.
ev.t_delator.note: Under the emperors, beginning with Tiberius, charges of maiestas (treason) became the weapon of informers - the delatores. By law the accuser received part of the convicted person's property, which turned denunciation into a profitable trade. Tacitus describes people tried for a careless word, a poem or a joke.
ev.t_delator.friend_at_court: Look for a protector at court
ev.t_delator.friend_at_court.success: An influential freedman of the emperor put in a word. The case was dropped, and the informer moved on to another victim.
ev.t_delator.friend_at_court.failure: The protector took the money and did nothing. The sentence: exile to an island and confiscation of half your property.
ev.t_delator.confess: Admit guilt and beg for mercy
ev.t_delator.confess.ok: You repented before the Senate, in tears. The emperor graciously settled for a heavy fine. Your friends now give you a wide berth.
ev.t_delator.counter.success: Your witnesses proved the joke had been twisted. The informer was convicted of slander, and you were awarded damages.
ev.t_delator.counter.failure: The countersuit was taken as insolence. The sentence: exile to an island and confiscation of most of your property.
ev.t_delator.retire: Withdraw to your estate and “fall ill”
ev.t_delator.retire.ok: You left for the Sabine hills and haven't shown your face in Rome. You've been forgotten - along with your business and your connections.
ev.t_exile_recall.title: Return from Exile
ev.t_exile_recall.text: A ship reached the island with news: the new emperor has pardoned those exiled under the old one. You return to Rome - older, but alive. Part of your property has even been returned.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.title: Proscriptions
ev.t_proscription_sulla.text: New lists have been posted in the Forum - and your name is on one. You were never Sulla's enemy, but one of his freedmen has taken a liking to your estate. The killer is promised a reward; your property will go to auction.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.note: In 82–81 BC the dictator Sulla published lists of the “proscribed”: they could be killed with impunity, a bounty was paid for their heads, and their property was auctioned. People were often added for the sake of their wealth - as in the case of Sextus Roscius, defended by the young Cicero.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.flee: Flee to the mountains at once
ev.t_proscription_sulla.flee.ok: You left that same night, in a slave's cloak, with a handful of coins. Others got your property, but you're alive.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.bribe.success: He took the money, and your name vanished from the lists as quietly as it appeared. You'll never know whose name went up in its place.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.bribe.failure: He took the money - and sent the killers. You fled through the garden, leaving everything.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.hide.success: A loyal slave brought you food in the tomb outside the city for a month. The storm passed, but the estate had already been plundered.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.hide.failure: You were betrayed. You tore free of the killers, wounded, and fled to the mountains, leaving everything you had.
ev.t_proscription_return.title: Amnesty
ev.t_proscription_return.text: Sulla has laid down his power, and fugitives are allowed to return. Your estate was sold off for a pittance long ago, and strangers live in it. You stand at the familiar gate, and not even the dog knows you.
ev.t_proscription_return.sue.success: The court ruled the sale unlawful. Part of your land came back to you - and your head spins as if after a long illness.
ev.t_proscription_return.sue.failure: The new owners are friends of powerful men. The case dragged on and came to nothing.
ev.t_proscription_return.start_over.ok: You rented a room in Rome and started from nothing. Sometimes that's easier than forever looking back.
ev.t_proscribed_master.title: The Master on the Lists
ev.t_proscribed_master.text: Your master's name is on the triumvirs' proscription lists. Heralds cry at every crossroads: a slave who betrays a proscribed man will get freedom, citizenship and a fortune. The master is hiding in the house, and only you know where.
ev.t_proscribed_master.note: In 43 BC Antony, Octavian and Lepidus declared proscriptions in which Cicero, among many others, died. A slave who betrayed his master was promised freedom, citizenship and a large reward. Appian tells of betrayals - and of slaves who hid their masters and even sacrificed themselves for them.
ev.t_proscribed_master.betray.ok: You showed the soldiers the way. The reward was paid in full: you're free and rich. Only at night you dream of that door creaking.
ev.t_proscribed_master.hide_master.succe: You got the master out of the city disguised as a porter and saw him onto a ship. When the storm passed he came back, and the first thing he did was set you free - with words you'll remember forever.
ev.t_proscribed_master.hide_master.failu: The soldiers found the hiding place. They took the master away, and beat you half to death for hiding him.
ev.t_proscribed_master.stay_out.ok: You pretended to know nothing. One morning the master was simply gone. What became of him, no one knows.
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.title: The Master's Son
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.text: After the amnesty the son of the man you once betrayed returned to Rome. He found you in your shop and silently laid an old key on the counter - the key to that very house.
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.beg.success: He was silent a long time, then said, “Back then everyone was saving their own skin.” And left. You feel lighter - a little.
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.beg.failure: He wouldn't listen. A month later your shop was wrecked, and the whole quarter calls you nothing but “the one who sold his master.”
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.leave.ok: You sold the shop in a hurry and moved to the port of Ostia. No one there knows who you are.
ev.t_land_confiscation.title: The Surveyors
ev.t_land_confiscation.text: Surveyors have come with poles and boundary stones: your district's land is being given to veterans. Your plot, where your ancestors' bones lie, goes to a former centurion - he's already been round to look, nodding approvingly.
ev.t_land_confiscation.note: In the 1st century BC generals paid their veterans in land: Sulla, Caesar and the triumvirs confiscated plots from Italian communities. The poet Virgil mourned such evictions in his Eclogues; according to tradition he managed to recover his own farm through Octavian's intervention.
ev.t_land_confiscation.plead: Go to Rome and plead for protection
ev.t_land_confiscation.plead.success: An influential man liked your bluntness. Your plot was struck off the lists - the centurion will get another.
ev.t_land_confiscation.plead.failure: You spent a month knocking on doors in Rome for nothing. When you got back, a stranger was on your field. You had to move to the city.
ev.t_land_confiscation.tenant: Stay on as the new owner's tenant
ev.t_land_confiscation.tenant.ok: You plow the same land - only now you hand half the harvest to a man who knows nothing about farming.
ev.t_land_confiscation.city: Take what they offer and go to Rome
ev.t_land_confiscation.city.ok: You loaded your belongings on a cart and went to Rome, where thousands like you look for day labor.
ev.t_land_confiscation.resist.success: The neighbors stood with you, and the veterans decided there was easier land to be had. They left you alone.
ev.t_land_confiscation.resist.failure: The veterans had fought for twenty years; you hadn't fought a day. They beat you and drove you off, and you reached Rome empty-handed.
ev.t_land_veteran.title: The Old Centurion
ev.t_land_veteran.text: The centurion who got your land has grown old, and he has no heirs. One evening he came to you himself. “The land is weeping without you. I don't know how to work it. Let's make a deal.”
ev.t_land_veteran.buy_back.ok: You gave everything you'd saved - and you stand on your own land as its master again. You plow the first furrow slowly, like a prayer.
ev.t_land_veteran.befriend.ok: You teach him to plow; he tells you about his wars. A strange friendship - but a strong one.
ev.t_land_veteran.refuse.ok: You said you don't buy what was stolen from you. The centurion nodded and left.
ev.t_province_governor.title: The Province
ev.t_province_governor.text: The lot has given you a province - for a year you'll be its governor, with lictors, troops and power over life and death. The elections cost you a fortune, and your creditors hint transparently: one is expected to come back from a province rich.
ev.t_province_governor.note: Governors of Roman provinces held nearly unlimited power and often enriched themselves at the provincials' expense. A special court existed for extortion cases; the most famous trial was Cicero's prosecution of Verres, governor of Sicily, in 70 BC. Verres went into exile without waiting for the verdict.
ev.t_province_governor.squeeze.ok: You came back with chests of silver, statues from other people's temples, and your debts paid in full. The provincials curse your name - in whispers, for now.
ev.t_province_governor.honest.ok: You judged fairly and took no gifts. You brought back almost no money, but the provincials walked you all the way to your ship.
ev.t_province_governor.decline.ok: You stayed in Rome. Your creditors are unhappy, the senators surprised, and your household delighted.
ev.t_repetundae.title: The Extortion Trial
ev.t_repetundae.text: The provincials sent an embassy to Rome, and an ambitious young orator has charged you with extortion. He's gathered mountains of evidence, and the whole Forum is talking about the trial.
ev.t_repetundae.advocate.success: Your advocate tangled the witnesses and moved the judges. Acquitted - though everyone knows how things really were.
ev.t_repetundae.advocate.failure: Even the best advocate couldn't save you. You're convicted, and there's only one thing left - exile.
ev.t_repetundae.exile.ok: You left before the verdict, taking what you could save. One can live in exile too - if one has money.
ev.t_repetundae.bribe_jury.success: A few purses passed at night did their work. Acquitted by a majority of two votes.
ev.t_repetundae.bribe_jury.failure: The bribery came to light. Now a new charge has been added to extortion, and you flee Rome.
ev.t_province_gratitude.title: Patron of a Province
ev.t_province_gratitude.text: An embassy has arrived from the province you once governed honestly: the city has chosen you as its patron, set up your statue in the agora, and sent gifts. An honest man can only dream of such a thing.
ev.t_charioteer.title: The Charioteer
ev.t_charioteer.text: A trainer for the Greens saw how you handle horses and wants to buy you for the circus. Charioteers die on the turns of the Circus Maximus, but the best of them are richer than senators, and all Rome knows their names.
ev.t_charioteer.note: Chariot racing in the Circus Maximus was Rome's great passion. Drivers, often slaves or freedmen, raced for the factions - Greens, Blues, Whites and Reds. The famous Gaius Appuleius Diocles won more than 1,400 races in the 2nd century AD and earned an enormous fortune.
ev.t_charioteer.race.success: You took the turn so close to the post that the stands gasped, and crossed the line first. A hundred thousand throats are shouting your name.
ev.t_charioteer.race.failure: On the seventh lap the chariot overturned. You survived, but you lay injured a long time, and the limp stayed.
ev.t_charioteer.bargain: Demand a share of the prizes
ev.t_charioteer.bargain.success: The trainer grumbled but agreed: part of the prize money goes into your peculium. Now you're racing for your freedom too.
ev.t_charioteer.bargain.failure: The trainer spat and bought someone else. Your master didn't forgive you for haggling.
ev.t_charioteer.stay.ok: You stayed with your master's horses. Safer - and quieter than the roar of the circus.
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.title: Darling of the Circus
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.text: After another victory the stands chanted “Freedom!” until the giver of the games nodded. Your master was paid, and you're free. What comes next is up to you.
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.keep_racing.ok: You signed with the faction as a free man. The prizes are yours now - all of them.
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.tavern: Buy a tavern by the circus
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.tavern.ok: You bought a tavern by the circus gates. Fans come in droves to drink with a living legend.
ev.t_love_gladiator.title: The Gladiator
ev.t_love_gladiator.text: You've lost your head over a gladiator - the one whose name is scrawled on the walls and who half the women of Rome sigh over. He wants you to run away with him to Capua. For a woman of your standing such an affair is a disgrace - and if it comes out, a trial and exile.
ev.t_love_gladiator.run_away.ok: You left it all - home, name, money - and went with him to Capua. In Rome they talk about you on every corner. You don't care.
ev.t_love_gladiator.secret.success: No one knows a thing. Your life has split in two, and the second half is the most alive.
ev.t_love_gladiator.secret.failure: A maid let it slip. A scandal across the city, divorce and disgrace - and a gladiator who didn't even come.
ev.t_love_gladiator.end.ok: You don't go to the amphitheater anymore. Sometimes, hearing his name, you leave the room.
ev.t_gladiator_falls.title: The Last Fight
ev.t_gladiator_falls.text: News came from the amphitheater: he fell in the arena. The crowd called for mercy, but the giver of the games gave no sign. You're alone in a strange city.
ev.t_gladiator_falls.go_home.ok: Your family took you back - with sighs, and without reproaches spoken aloud. Rome forgave the scandal faster than you forgave yourself.
ev.t_gladiator_falls.stay.ok: His comrades from the school took up a collection for you. You stayed in Capua - here at least they remember his name.
ev.t_nexum.title: Debt Bondage
ev.t_nexum.text: The bad harvest has eaten all your stores. The patrician moneylender will give grain and money only under nexum: if you don't repay on time, you'll work off the debt in his house - in chains, if he chooses. Your household is hungry, and he's in no hurry.
ev.t_nexum.note: The early Roman Republic knew nexum - debt bondage in which the debtor pledged his own person and could be put in chains by the creditor. According to tradition it was abolished by the Lex Poetelia around 326 BC, after plebeian anger reached a breaking point. The details come mainly from Livy.
ev.t_nexum.bind.ok: You swore before witnesses with bronze and scales. There's grain, and no one at home goes hungry. And the deadline is already dripping away like a water clock.
ev.t_nexum.sell_land.ok: You sold your father's plot to a patrician neighbor. Now you're free - and you hire yourself out to him as a day laborer.
ev.t_nexum.colony: Sign up for a new colony
ev.t_nexum.colony.ok: Rome is founding a colony on conquered land, and the settlers get plots. You leave with a hundred others like you - to start from nothing on the frontier.
ev.t_nexum.clan_patron: Ask your clan's patron for help
ev.t_nexum.clan_patron.success: The patron helped with grain, no bondage - in exchange for loyalty and your vote in the assembly. That's a chain too, but a softer one.
ev.t_nexum.clan_patron.failure: The patron was busy with his own affairs and wouldn't even see you. You went home with nothing.
ev.t_nexum_end.title: The Debt Falls Due
ev.t_nexum_end.text: The term of the debt has run out, and there's no money. The moneylender has come with men and chains: by law you now belong to him until you've worked it off.
ev.t_nexum_end.pay.ok: You scraped together every last coin. The chains stayed with the moneylender, and you stayed home.
ev.t_nexum_end.work_off: Work it off in his house
ev.t_nexum_end.work_off.ok: For two years you worked in his house like a slave and slept in the stocks. You came out free - but a different person.
ev.t_nexum_end.tribunes: Appeal to the tribunes of the plebs
ev.t_nexum_end.tribunes.success: You showed the crowd in the Forum the scars from the chains. The plebs roared, the tribunes intervened, and the moneylender backed down.
ev.t_nexum_end.tribunes.failure: The tribunes listened but couldn't help. The moneylender took you away, and freedom was a long way off.
ev.t_monsoon_india.title: The Wind to India
ev.t_monsoon_india.text: Pilots know the secret: in summer the wind blows east off the sea so steadily that a ship from the Red Sea ports reaches India in forty days - and comes back on the winter wind with pepper, pearls and silk. One voyage can make you rich - or you may never return.
ev.t_monsoon_india.note: Around the end of the 2nd century BC Greek sailors learned to use the monsoon winds to cross the open sea from Egypt to India. Ships sailed from Berenice and Myos Hormos to Muziris and other ports; the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (1st century AD) describes the route, and Pliny complains of how much Roman gold flowed east.
ev.t_monsoon_india.go.success: A year later you returned to Alexandria sunburned, with sacks of pepper and stories of elephants and temples. The goods sold for five times the price. You're rich now.
ev.t_monsoon_india.go.failure: The ship lost its mast off Arabia. You returned nearly two years later, sick and empty-handed.
ev.t_monsoon_india.invest.success: The ship came back, and your share of the pepper brought in more than you'd earned in years.
ev.t_monsoon_india.invest.failure: The ship never returned. People say all sorts of things about it, but talk won't bring the money back.
ev.t_monsoon_india.stay.ok: You watched the sails go. Some will return rich; some won't return at all.
ev.t_india_friend.title: A Guest from Muziris
ev.t_india_friend.text: In Alexandria's harbor an Indian merchant sought you out - you once drank wine together on the Malabar coast. He's brought a shipload of spices and proposes a deal: his goods, your connections.
ev.t_india_friend.partner.success: The spices sold within a month. You swore to each other by all your gods and planned a new voyage.
ev.t_india_friend.partner.failure: Customs took a quarter of the value in duty, and the warehouse got damp. You split the loss evenly - as friends.
ev.t_india_friend.decline.ok: You drank to old times, and he sailed off with another partner.
ev.t_anachoresis.title: Fleeing the Taxes
ev.t_anachoresis.text: There's no way to pay this year's tax, and the collector has already promised debtors' prison. Two neighbors vanished last month - gone to the Delta marshes, where the reeds are taller than a man and officials never go. The old folk say people did the same under the pharaohs.
ev.t_anachoresis.note: Peasants fleeing their villages - anachoresis in Greek - was a common response to heavy taxes and compulsory labor in Ptolemaic and Roman Egypt. Fugitives hid in the Delta marshes, in temples with the right of asylum, or in other districts. The authorities alternately punished them and proclaimed pardons: a decree of 118 BC, for example, allowed fugitives to return without penalty.
ev.t_anachoresis.flee.ok: You slipped away at night by boat down the canal. Other fugitives live in the reeds: they cut papyrus, catch fish and pay nobody.
ev.t_anachoresis.asylum: Take refuge in a temple with right of asylum
ev.t_anachoresis.asylum.success: The priests let you inside the precinct wall, where collectors may not go. You'll wait here until the storm blows over.
ev.t_anachoresis.asylum.failure: The guards dragged you out of the temple courtyard despite the priests' shouts. Debtors' prison, and an inventory of everything you own.
ev.t_anachoresis.endure.ok: You did your time in debtors' prison and your belongings were auctioned. You came out sick and poor - but in your own village.
ev.t_anachoresis.bribe.success: The collector took the money and listed you as “without means.” You're safe for a year.
ev.t_anachoresis.bribe.failure: The collector took the money - and seized your property anyway. There's no one to complain to.
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.title: A Decree of Pardon
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.text: Word has reached the marshes: a decree has been posted - fugitives may return to their villages, and the debts of past years are forgiven. Some are already readying boats; others don't believe a word the officials say.
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.return.ok: You returned to your kin, and the village scribe wrote you back onto the rolls. The decree didn't lie - this time.
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.stay_marsh.ok: Here you've learned to weave papyrus mats and bow to no one. You have no wish to go back under someone else's rule.
ev.t_auxilia.title: Twenty-Five Years
ev.t_auxilia.text: Roman recruiters have come to the village. An auxiliary cohort or the fleet: twenty-five years of service, and then Roman citizenship, a bronze tablet with your name, and money for your old age. Your mother is crying and holding your hand.
ev.t_auxilia.note: Provincials, Egyptians among them, served in Rome's auxiliary forces and fleet. After 25–26 years of service a veteran received Roman citizenship, confirmed by a bronze “military diploma.” Many veterans settled in Egypt - for example at Karanis in the Fayum - and became prosperous landowners.
ev.t_auxilia.cohort.ok: They gave you a shield, a spear and a new Roman name for the rolls. Ahead: desert, garrisons and a quarter century of service.
ev.t_auxilia.fleet.ok: They sent you to a ship. You knew the Nile; now you'll learn the sea - for the next twenty-five years.
ev.t_auxilia.refuse.ok: You stayed in the village. Your mother stopped crying, and the recruiters moved on to the neighbors.
ev.t_auxilia_discharge.title: The Bronze Tablet
ev.t_auxilia_discharge.text: A quarter century is behind you. You've been handed a bronze tablet: from now on you're a Roman citizen, a right your descendants will inherit. With your discharge money you buy land in the Fayum, where other veterans live, and the peasant neighbors bow to you in the street.
